A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SEVAL paper with 33 readable pages, including Appendices A–D. Complete text comparison and rendered-page checks establish that differences are confined to the version stamp and Appendix C.2.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original SEVAL benchmark, ablation, sensitivity and integration experiments. Appendix C.3 explicitly identifies the Semi-Aves experiments as conducted by the authors.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark evaluations and the additional experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2, Equation (26), corrects the stated grouped-threshold calculation: v1 sums class-specific optimizer outputs, whereas v2 performs one optimization against pooled group accuracy. This is a localized procedural correction; the PDFs do not establish changed code or rerun experiments.

E1.justification: Both retain CIFAR10-LT, CIFAR100-LT, STL10-LT, Semi-Aves with and without open-set unlabelled data, Small-ImageNet-127, and the two-moons scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments, including the DARP, FlexMatch, FreeMatch and other comparisons in Table 2, and the DASO comparisons across SSL frameworks in Table 9.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–C retain the same data splits, preprocessing, model architectures, training budgets and evaluation metrics. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 6, post-hoc adjustment and validation-size analyses in Figure 4, Appendix B.1 sensitivity analysis, and Appendix D class-performance analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the Section 5 statement that average test accuracy and variance are derived from three random seeds. Uncertainty reporting and the reported uncertainty entries are unchanged.

E6.justification: All empirical entries and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains SEVAL's 82.8 ± 0.56 in its first CIFAR10-LT setting, and Table 8 retains 34.8 averaged class recall on Small-ImageNet-127.

T1.justification: Equation (26) moves the class summation from outside the argmin into the accuracy term inside the absolute-error objective. This is a non-equivalent mathematical correction. The main theoretical statements and Appendix A proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about learning refinement offsets and thresholds from labelled training partitions and improving imbalanced SSL.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning precision, recall, calibration and applicability remain unchanged. The rewritten Appendix C.2 sentence retains the existing difficulty with sparse minority-class samples and the same zero-threshold fallback.

D1.justification: The Equation (26) correction in the implementation appendix clarifies how class counts must be aggregated when implementing a shared group threshold. Other implementation instructions, Table 10 hyperparameters and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the reference list are unchanged. There is no revision to novelty positioning or relationships with prior methods.

P1.justification: A sentence about scarce minority-class samples in Appendix C.2 receives a grammatical rewrite, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Terminology and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–11 retain their formatting, captions and placement. The overall page layout and organization are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation (26) replaces a sum of optimizer outputs with a single optimization of pooled group accuracy, matching the stated shared-threshold construction. This provides a limited improvement in mathematical consistency and reproducibility. The empirical evidence and broader claims remain unchanged.
